'''Digvijaysinh Pratapsinhji Jhala'''  (20 August 1932 – 4 April 2021) was an Indian politician from [[Gujarat]]. He served as India's first environment minister in the central government.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/former-union-minister-digvijaysinh-zala-passes-away-at-88/articleshow/81894905.cms | title=Former Union Minister Digvijaysinh Zala passes away at 88 | publisher=[[The Economic Times]] | date=4 April 2021 | accessdate=4 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/indias-first-environment-minister-digvijaysinh-jhala-dies-at-89-7258530/lite/ | title=India's first environment minister Digvijaysinh Jhala dies at 89 | publisher=The Indian Express | date=4 April 2021 | accessdate=4 April 2021}}</ref>

==Early life==
Jhala was born at [[Ranjit Vilas Palace (Wankaner)|Ranjit Vilas Palace]] at [[Wankaner]] on 20 August 1932, the eldest son of [[Pratapsinhji Jhala]] of the princely state of Wankaner, by his wife, Sisodiji Maharani Sri Rama Kanwar Sahiba.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

He was educated at [[Rajkumar College, Rajkot]] and graduated from [[Cambridge University]], and obtained a doctorate from [[Delhi University|Delhi University's]] [[St Stephen's College, Delhi|St Stephen's College]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

==Family==
In 1955, Jhala married Maharajkumari Baiji Lal Pratap Kumari Sahiba, eldest daughter of [[Tej Singh Prabhakar|Sir Tej Singhji]], Maharaja of [[Alwar State]]. Jhala married again in 1982, to Vibha Singh, daughter of a senior bureaucrat and diplomat Shri Bhagwan Singh. She was media personality and also served as a consul general of Nauru. Jhala and Vibha's only son, Kesarisihji, was born in 1983. Kesarisihji is nominated as Rajysabha Member of Parliament from [[Bharatiya Janta Party]] and elections are awaiting.<ref name=x/>

==Wankaner State==
Jhala was heir apparent to the throne of the princely state of Wankaner at birth, holding the title [[Yuvaraja|Yuvraj Sahib]] of Wankaner officially from 1932, when the State merged with newly independent India. He succeeded his father in 2007 as the titular King of Wankaner and head of its royal house.<ref>{{cite news|title=Royal regrets selling Wankaner House to US govt|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/Royal-regrets-selling-Wankaner-House-to-US-govt/articleshow/10686285.cms|accessdate=19 August 2016|publisher=Times of India|date=11 November 2011}}</ref>

==Political career==
Jhala entered politics after the independence of India and joined the [[Indian National Congress]]. He was a Member of Legislative Assembly for [[Wankaner]] in the [[Gujarat Legislative Assembly]] for the years 1962-67 and 1967–71. He was then elected [[Member of parliament, Lok Sabha|Member of Parliament]] for [[Surendranagar]] for two terms, from 1980 to 1989.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} He also served as the Union Deputy Minister for Ecology and the Environment from 1982 to 1984.<ref name=x>{{cite news|title=Gujarat ex-royals project Modi as PM-in-waiting|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/gujarat-exroyals-project-modi-as-pminwaiting/806027/|accessdate=19 August 2016|agency=The Indian Express|date=20 June 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Short term plans, long term disasters|url=http://www.indiaenvironmentportal.org.in/content/23501/short-term-plans-long-term-disasters/|website=India Environment Portal|accessdate=19 August 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Being very active in public life, Jhala was also Convener of the Indian Heritage Hotels Association, Gujarat, Chairman of Gujarat Hotels Association and President of the Wankaner Co-op Agricultural Bank Ltd for 1962–1964.

He was Director of Shree Amarsinhji Mills Ltd since 1960, a cotton textile mill founded in 1951 by his grandfather [[Amarsinhji Banesinhji|Sir Amarsinhji Banesinhji]], which was later taken over by [[Kores (company)|Kores India]] in 1980.

He served as a director of [[India Tourism Development Corporation]] for the years 1968–1982.

He was a founder member of the Indigenous Horse Society of India founded in 1999. He was also a member of the Gujarat State Water Pollution Control Board since 1976, National Committee for Environmental Planning since 1981 and president of the [[Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha]] since 1989.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.akhilbharatiyakshatriyamahasabha.com/ |title=Home |website=akhilbharatiyakshatriyamahasabha.com}}</ref>

Jhala died on 4 April 2021 at the age of 88, after a brief illness.<ref>{{Cite news|last=ANI|date=2021-04-04|title=Ex-Union Minister Digvijaysinh Zala passes away at 88 after brief illness|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/ex-union-minister-digvijaysinh-zala-passes-away-at-88-after-brief-illness-121040400137_1.html|access-date=2021-04-04}}</ref>
